steps.body: Stories name the whole and the pieces in words: read for how many EQUAL pieces the whole became, then how many the story is about.
steps.narration: Stories name the whole and the pieces in words: read for how many EQUAL pieces the whole became, then how many the story is about.

widget.prompt: A ribbon is cut into 6 equal pieces and 5 are used. Build the fraction used.
widget.successFeedback: 5/6 — six equal pieces made, five of them used.
widget.lowFeedback: Your shaded bar is shorter than the target half. Shade more — raise the numerator, or use fewer parts.
widget.highFeedback: Your shaded bar is longer than half. Shade less — lower the numerator, or split into more parts.

commonFractions.feedback: That flipped the numbers: sixths are the piece size, so 6 belongs underneath.
1/6 names a single piece, but five pieces were used.

predict.prompt: A ribbon in 6 equal pieces, 5 used. Which number goes on the bottom?
predict.reveal: The bottom always names how many equal pieces the whole became; the top counts the ones in question.

cml.actionGoal: Cut, count, and compare equal pieces to see what g3f story really names.
invariants: A fraction names equal shares of ONE whole: the denominator says how many equal pieces the whole became, and the numerator counts them, which is what makes g3f story comparable at all.
misconceptions: Calling unequal pieces fractions, reading the denominator as a count, or comparing fractions that came from different-sized wholes.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the whole changed size, which of these comparisons would stop being trustworthy?

widget.prompt: A ribbon is cut into 6 equal pieces and 5 are used. Which fraction names what was used?

options.label: 5/6 — five of six equal pieces
options.feedback: Correct — the denominator counts the equal pieces the whole became, and the numerator counts the ones used.

options.label: 6/5 — six pieces, five used
options.feedback: That puts the whole on top; the piece count belongs underneath, and 6/5 would be more than one ribbon.

options.label: 1/6 — one piece was used
options.feedback: 1/6 names a single piece, but five of them were used, not one.

options.label: 1/5 — five pieces
options.feedback: The ribbon was cut into SIX pieces, so sixths are the piece size no matter how many were used.

widget.prompt: A trail is 4/6 mile, then 1/6 mile more. Express the total as ?/6. What is the numerator?

commonErrors.feedback: 6 names the piece size; adding same-size pieces changes only how MANY you have.
Multiplying the counts is not joining them — 4 pieces and 1 more pieces make 5.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Name the equal pieces the whole was cut into, then count how many of them the question is about.

commonErrors.feedback: 16 counts the PIECES. Every 8 of them rebuild one whole, so ask how many groups of 8 fit.
8 is the piece size, not how many wholes 16 pieces make.
